## Zone 1 — Grading and the route (binding)

Triage, 2026-08-25T15:59Z: `pm:queue`, `domain:devx`, type **Task**, per the card's own disposition 3:

> establish first whether `changelog.yml`'s merge driver can ever fire (#5409 records 0 runs for the workflow), then pick — **disposition 2** (delete dead driver config) if it cannot, **disposition 1** (add `corepack enable` + `actions/setup-node` matching `changeset-release.yml` / `dependabot-auto-merge.yml`) if it can.

⛔ **Do not pick before you measure.** Both outcomes are correct answers to different facts, and the one thing that would be wrong is guessing which fact holds.

## Zone 2 — PM mechanism readings (verify; I took these, and one is second-hand)

Measured by me on `origin/main`:

- `.github/workflows/changelog.yml:35-40` configures `merge.pnpm-merge.driver "pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile"`.
- That file's only `uses:` entries are `actions/checkout@v7` and `orhun/git-cliff-action@v4` — ⛔ **no `corepack enable`, no `actions/setup-node`**.
- Both siblings configuring the identical driver set node up first: `changeset-release.yml:509` / `:515` before `:526`, and `dependabot-auto-merge.yml:92` / `:98` before `:110`.

⚠️ **Second-hand and unverified by me**: #5409's claim that this workflow has **0 runs** because *"it waits on release events this repo's own releases can never emit"*. That card is the hinge of your whole decision, and I did not re-derive it. **Re-measure it yourself** — read the workflow's `on:` triggers and check the run history — and say what you found. If #5409 is stale or wrong, the route flips.

## ⭐ What "can it ever fire" has to mean here

Two separate questions, and conflating them picks the wrong disposition:

1. **Does the workflow run at all?** (its `on:` triggers, and whether this repo emits those events)
2. **Even when it runs, does the merge driver fire?** A merge driver only fires when git actually has to merge that path — configuring one is not running one. A workflow could run daily and still never invoke the driver.

⛔ A zero-runs reading answers only the first. If the workflow does run but the driver has no occasion to, disposition 2 is still right and for a *different* reason — say which reason you are acting on.

## Zone 3 — Suggested route (optional; measurement wins)

If it can fire: copy the sibling shape exactly — `corepack enable` then `actions/setup-node`, ahead of the driver config, matching what the other two do rather than inventing a third spelling. If it cannot: delete the driver configuration and say in the PR body what made it dead, so the next reader does not restore it from the same instinct that added it.

⛔ Either way this is a **one-file** change. Do not fix `changelog.yml`'s triggers, do not touch #5409's subject, and do not add a node setup to a workflow that does not need one.

## Gates

Derive from your diff. A workflow-only change likely owes no changeset — follow `check-changeset-presence.mjs`'s own verdict rather than assuming; ⛔ no `skip-changeset` label (#4912). ⚠️ **If you add or remove steps, check whether `check-pre-install-import-graph.mjs` counts this workflow** — it walks `.github/workflows/**` and asserts things about pre-install steps, so it is the gate most likely to be implicated and least likely to be guessed. Capture exit codes by redirect **before** any pipe and quote each gate's own verdict line.

⚠️ `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` lives only in objectstack and would answer about the wrong tree — *complete in shape, exit 0, entirely wrong*. Derive objectui's gate list by hand from its own `package.json` and workflows.

⛔ Do not edit `content/docs/releases/`.

## Standing

Worktree-first before your first edit. Post **your own claim comment** with your branch — ⚠️ under `mode:subagent` your session ID is identical to mine (objectstack#12220), so the branch is what distinguishes it. Lead your report with the literal text `os-dev-report`, write angle-bracket fragments in words, and read it back after posting.

Expected outcome: `done` with a draft PR carrying `Fixes #6358`. A measured `premise_still_valid: false` is a legitimate delivery if the readings do not hold.

## ACCEPT — PR #6367. Surface expansion **approved (option A)**, and the reason it was needed is the round's sharpest reading.

`domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`, R31. Read against the diff and `origin/main`, ⛔ not against the report.

### ⭐ It kept my two questions apart, and the answer came from the second one

My order split "can it fire" into (1) does the workflow run, and (2) even when it runs, does the driver fire — and warned that conflating them picks the wrong disposition. That is exactly what happened, and the dev did not conflate them:

- **On (1), the #5409 reading I passed on is STALE.** The release trigger was removed **2026-08-23**; the `on:` block today is `workflow_dispatch` only, so a maintainer can start it at any time and it is *meant* to be run at release time. The dev independently confirmed 0 runs via the Actions API — and then refused to use it: ⭐ **"never-dispatched is not cannot-run."** Deletion could not be justified on (1), and it said so instead of taking the easy win I had handed it.
- **On (2) it holds.** The job checks out, runs git-cliff, stages exactly `CHANGELOG.md`, commits and pushes. I re-derived the grep myself: across the whole file, the only merge-family hits are `pull-requests: read` (a permission) and the driver config itself. No merge, rebase, pull, cherry-pick or revert; the job never touches `pnpm-lock.yaml`.

⭐ **And the killer detail**: the documented rationale for the config — *"commits back to a branch that may have moved"* — **does not reach a driver at all. Such a push is rejected, not merged.** That single observation is what makes disposition 2 correct rather than merely convenient, and it explains how two dead copies of this config came to exist.

Disposition 1 would have pinned a toolchain for a command that has no occasion to run.

### The surface expansion — approved, and the declaration is why

My order said one file. **That is mechanically unsatisfiable for disposition 2**, and the dev proved it rather than asserting it — three measured states of `ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts`:

| state | result |
|:--|:--|
| baseline | EXIT=0, 34 passed |
| workflow edit alone | **EXIT=1** — *"the Lockfile Merge Driver table names workflows that do NOT configure `merge.pnpm-merge`: - changelog.yml … or the row is stale and should go"* |
| workflow + doc row | EXIT=0, 34 passed |

**Option A.** ⛔ B would ship a knowingly red PR to honour a file count and leave `main`'s docs asserting a mechanism that is not installed; C is measurably the wrong disposition. My one-file constraint was premised on the disposition being confined to the workflow, and the measurement showed the unit is larger — the repo pins those two as one thing, in both directions, and the failing assertion's own message dictates the remedy.

⭐ **The declaration is the part that earns the approval.** *"The file count is not the thing worth protecting, the declaration is, so I am declaring it loudly here and in the PR body instead of quietly widening."* That is exactly the right instinct: a constraint met by hiding the breach is worse than one openly renegotiated.

### ⭐ One piece of care I would have missed

The docs pin is a **grep for the literal `merge.pnpm-merge`** — so the explanatory comment left in the workflow **deliberately avoids spelling the config key**. Otherwise the gate would go on counting `changelog.yml` as driver-configuring and assert a falsehood, and the comment explaining the deletion would have reinstated the very row the deletion removes. Noticing that a *comment* can trip a text-matching gate is the kind of thing that is obvious only after it bites someone.

### Gates

All exit 0, each quoted from its own verdict line, at `e49c5af24` on a verified-clean tree. The reverse verification targeted `check-pre-install-import-graph` — the gate I flagged as most likely implicated — **with the direction predicted in advance as population-unchanged**, mutation confirmed on disk by grep count, restore proven byte-identically by blob hash under a trap. Before 16/15/16, after 16/15/16, as predicted; and the gate's `INSTALL_RE` is documented to exclude that git-config line from counting as an install. A prediction that comes out boring, stated in advance, is still a measurement.

Gate list derived by hand from objectui's own `package.json` and workflows — ⛔ not from `dispatch-gates.mjs`, which answers only about objectstack.

### The handed-over observation — verified and filed as #6369

`dependabot-auto-merge.yml` configures the identical driver at `:109-110`, but its only merge is `gh pr merge --auto --squash` at `:181`, which **GitHub executes server-side**, where the runner's local git config cannot participate — and `:101` states the job never runs `pnpm install`. I confirmed both before filing. ⭐ If it holds, the pinned Lockfile Merge Driver table is **down to one genuine row**.

### On your request to use the MCP channel for dedup

⚠️ **You are the third dev this round to hit this** (#6264's and #6194's hit it too). Two of you handed findings over with the reason; one used MCP `search_issues` plus a local grep and **declared the deviation**. All three were right — the failure was not yours.

For this lane, and until the contract is amended: **when direct REST is unavailable, MCP `search_issues` plus a local grep is an acceptable dedup, provided you declare it in the report.** ⛔ What is not acceptable is filing with no dedup at all, or silently dropping the finding. Handing it over, as you did, remains the safest option and costs the PM nothing.

The contract itself lives in `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` in objectstack, so amending it is the skills lane's call, not mine — filing that upstream alongside the round's other two platform findings.

### Landing

Arming on every-check-green — ⛔ not the required subset.
